citations.review_text: DO NOT GET THIS GAME IF YOU WANT A CLEAR PATH. But, if you enjoy games where you're just dropped into the world, like hk, this game might be perfect for you. Also it has beautiful graphics and art styles!
I dont know what to do in this game.

claims.claim: Keyboard and mouse controls are poorly implemented for PC.

citations.review_text:
it's pretty good.
I could never get into Dark Souls and Demon Souls style game. But this one is clicking with me.

It's a very game controller oriented game, KB+M controls are shit.

key bindings suck 
ambient music sucks for ~95% of the game,
no way to pause (doubly suck with the ambient music)
so much junk in my inventory
The openworld is cool, but you also end up spending hours upon hours and make no progress because your build does not need that one stupid item you found. this is also stupid because the first 4 bosses I found were stupidly hard... turns out I just happen to find all the hardest bosses around the starting area.
yes you can just lookup easier bosses and an OP build and easy mode the game but that is also stupid. 

I will still probably play the game but it is a LOT worse than expected and I bought it at full price thinking it is a well proven good game.

Man, I really want to like this game. I have a ton of respect for From Software and the worlds they have built over the years, though this is my first time actually playing one of their games (besides armored core VI, which I loved). I have watched countless lore videos on every single one of their games over the years. I really want to dive deep into the world of elden ring, but what holds me back from both playing and being able to recommend this game for mouse and keyboard players such as myself are the downright ATROCIOUS controls/camera design, that have no options for changing. 

Why does left click cause me to swing my weapon on the RIGHT side of torrent, and why does right click swing my weapon on the LEFT side of torrent? Why does a heavy attack actually swing on the correct side of torrent in regards to if you do a left or right heavy attack?

Why does the camera lock feature constantly lock me onto enemies I don't want to be locked on if it detects the slightest input from my mouse? Why cant I just lock onto a single enemy, and only unlock from that one enemy by dragging my mouse away, disengaging target locking as a whole? Why am I forced to hold my mouse 90 degrees relative to my computer desk to stay locked onto a single enemy while my camera goes haywire tracking it inside of a small room as it jumps around like crazy? Even fighting outside especially in the case of trolls, I am constantly fighting my mouse to stay locked onto a single leg instead of locking on to like 3 other body parts constantly, all the while trying to stay under/behind it to avoid its attacks, while my camera is spinning all over the place like crazy. 

Why cant I rebind dodge and sprint to different buttons? In helldivers 2 for example, I love being able to dive with the left alt key. In every game that has a dodge or dive feature, I always rebind that action to alt. It is extremely convenient to hit with your left thumb and it instantly eliminates the possibility of accidentall…

The game is pretty fun although I would most likely have dropped it if I did not have a friend who can explain some stuff and give some pointers. It's too easy to miss quests or important items making you feel quite stuck without needing outside help.

The camera can sometimes make me motion sick which is not something I ususally have issues with, so keep this in mind if you're someone who gets motion sick easily.

claims.claim: PC performance suffers from stutters, frame rate issues, or data loss crashes.

citations.review_text: The game is fun and all. But the game suffers greatly with data loss in the big 2026 for some reason - my game crashed and I lost 5 hours of gameplay.

This is probably gonna be the only actual serious review I do, and it's because I love Elden Ring to the bottom of my heart. This is a game that came out during one of my darkest times, and I genuinely feel like it saved me.

Having played this originally on PS4 and then PS5, I have a solid 400 to 500 hours in it. That might not be a lot to some people, but it means everything to me. Despite that, I simply cannot recommend this game on PC. FromSoftware are masterclass, top dogs when it comes to creating breathtaking, jaw-dropping worlds and overall design. They are one of the most talented studios out there, and I'm glad this game achieved the massive success it did. So why the negative review?

For some reason, this game just does not work properly on PC. The performance is so laughably bad it physically hurts. A huge part of the problem comes down to how poorly Easy Anti-Cheat is implemented, alongside FromSoftware seemingly refusing to get a PC port right. The game constantly conflicts with CPU Core 0 and other background tasks, causing severe shader compilation stutters and making the FPS drop like a nuke falling out of an airplane. On top of that, standard PC features like an unlocked frame rate or ultrawide support are completely missing.

The worst part is that there is no real way to fix these stutters without relying on community modders, just like Dark Souls 1 all over again. Even worse, using mods to fix the performance forces you to play offline, locking you out of coop, messages, and pvp just to get a smooth frame rate. In this day and age, it is completely unacceptable for a game to run this poorly on an RTX 3090 and an i7-12700K, even with RT turned off. Play this masterpiece on console if you can, because the PC port does not do it justice.

Fine game, sadly being "console first" gives it a bunch of very dogshit issues. 

- Bad frame pacing and horrible post effects cause motion sickness, i assume cause this was either badly play-tested or play-tested on console with display relatively far away. 

- Horrible control out of the box for keyboard. Xbox controller expected cause of course it is, we all like sticking our butts up for the Microslop company. 

- The game is locked in 60FPS (for some god damn reason , due to how its coded and due to consoles sadly still existing i suppose) when 120, 144+ Hz monitors are common nowadays. You can mod it out of the game by hex editing the .exe but that's not really an excuse. 

Beside that game is fine-ish, the world is cool. But for this price they didn't even lift their ass to polish it for PC market, and just fed us a pre-release like slop. God bless modders though for fixing this crap. 

10/10 of Stinky Japanese Mega-corporations for this "AAA" Duracell battery experience.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players find complex quest lines challenging to navigate without outside help.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that NPC quests and storylines are difficult to follow or comprehend without consulting external guides.

citations.review_text: I wouldn't recommend this game to most people and that is why I am selecting the thumbs down button. Although this game is something of an achievement and can be very engaging for the right people, I don't think most people will really enjoy most of it or finish it. They'll just spend their time running past enemies, dodging them to get to the good parts. And the "good parts" are just a whole lot of inching forward and playing the same areas over and over unless you consult a guide. The story, quests and NPCs in the game are almost incomprehensible - you'll just happen to progress NPC's quests by chance unless you are paying extreme attention to everything or else following a guide. I do find the graphics, art, music and other aspects very nice but overall it's just kind of a large lonely static somber world that just takes too much time and effort for the average player to enjoy. Plan on putting 100-150 hours into this game, not including the DLC, if you do decide to take the plunge.

I put this game off forever because I knew my temper had no business near a FromSoftware title.
Can confirm: I have wanted to put my fist through my monitor on multiple occasions.

That being said, it is an absolute joy to play. The open world is visually stunning, the boss fights and combat mechanics are incredible once they click, and there’s an absurd amount of loot and gear to track down. The story is completely incomprehensible without reading guides and wikis, but I can live with that.

I hate this game. Can't wait to play it some more.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the massive, detailed world despite recycled encounters.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world and its regions offer immense exploration, vast landscapes, and dense detail.

citations.review_text: A genuine masterpiece. I can confidently say I've never enjoyed a game quite as much as Elden Ring. Between its incredible world-building, breathtaking scenery, rewarding exploration, and sheer freedom of choice, there's always something new to discover. Even after countless playthroughs, the Lands Between never cease to amaze me. An unforgettable experience and an absolute must-play.

I’ve played this game for the first time and I can finally understand the hype. Each region feels like its own little world and the game allows you total freedom about where to go and what to do. A true masterpiece

I have nearly 300 hours in this game and I have the platinum but the game is just so vast and dense in detail, that I can always find something new. The first 10 hours of playing this game made me want to commit atrocities but after the rough start when you actually begin to play and not just die every 17 seconds. it becomes magnificent. All in all, the game is just simply amazing.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that certain bosses and minor bosses are reused throughout the world.

citations.review_text: A truly incredible experience, it builds on the existing Soulsborne legacy and makes something that still feels unique. It does struggle to keep things fair on a few bosses and does repeat some minor bosses, but despite that it is still an incredible experience.

Plenty of bullshit that's easy to hate, and rightfully so. It's far from the perfection that people like to pretend it is. But it's still real good. Amazing world design, great build variety to have fun with, and some great bosses. Just make sure you don't take too much damage from any of those bosses (bosses that get reused ten thousand times), because then you'll have to heal. And if you dare to press that button? Lmao. Prepare for the boss to drop their 50 hit combo that you managed to dodge out of, teleport to you at light speed, and instantly start another 50 hit combo that will catch you before you can dodge out of your heal.

Elden Ring gives you a breathtaking fantasy world, complete freedom, and a guy on a horse whose sole purpose is to remind you that you're not the main character.

Welcome to the Lands Between. Your confidence has left the chat.

The exploration is phenomenal. Every castle, cave, and suspicious-looking elevator might lead to something incredible or something that kills you before you finish saying "What's that?"

Combat is challenging but rewarding, build variety is fantastic, and some bosses are genuinely unforgettable. Few games make overcoming a difficult encounter feel this satisfying.

But it's not flawless. Recycled bosses and dungeons eventually become noticeable, quests can be absurdly cryptic, and the camera occasionally decides the real boss fight should be against your own eyesight. PC performance has also had its rough moments.

Ratings:

Gameplay: 9.5/10

World & Exploration: 10/10

Story & Lore: 9/10

Graphics & Art Direction: 9/10

Enjoyment: 9.5/10

Elden Ring doesn't hold your hand. It breaks it, sends you exploring, and somehow convinces you to thank it afterward.

Overall: 9.5/10 | Highly Recommended

citations.review_text:
A most worthy tale,

Fellow tarnished give ear unto mine account, for never hath a game so stirred my soul. In the beginning I was but a wretch, felled again and again by beasts, but with each Site of Grace last rested upon, each foe at last overcome, I grew mightier. No victory is granted freely. And as my strength grew, so too did my heart for those I met upon my journey.

Noble warrior Alexander sought only to become a greater warrior. And of course Malenia the Blade of Miquella, who hath slew me more times than I can number. In battle I cursed her name, but in learning her tale I came to pity her, for being cursed at birth with a rot she never chose. And yet she still fought, loyal to her brother until the very last.

Each soul beareth a story, and each story ends with meaning. Be it joyous or sorrowful

single_points.text: One reviewer says that without ever touching Multiplayer with the mods and only ever using them in Singleplayer, they got banned from Multiplayer for 180 days.

citation.review_text: I like this game, really. It's been really fun I even started NG+2 (vanilla). I later wanted to mod the game to try out the amazing mods the community made, that extended the functionality and it was fun. But the Anti-Cheat is shitty. Without ever touching Multiplayer with the mods and only ever using them in Singleplayer, I got banned from Multiplayer for 180 days. Nice job FromSoftware. You made such a great game, but fu***ed up the Anti-Cheat situation, how is something like that possible? But I guess as long as players don't use mods, its still a great game, so I'm still recommending this game. Not that I like that part, but it is what it is.
